history.period: Believed over 700 years old (unverified); idols relocated 1964
history.summary: A Hanuman shrine about 2 km from the Ramanathaswamy Temple on the Rameswaram-Thangachimadam road (near Letchumanan Theertham), famous for its floating stones. The 18-20 ft five-faced Hanuman idol (Hanuman, Narasimha, Garuda, Varaha, Hayagriva) is believed over 700 years old and was relocated here from Dhanushkodi after the 1964 cyclone, along with idols of Rama and Sita. The 'floating stones' (sethu bandanam) kept in water tanks are traditionally held to be from the Ram Setu built by the vanara sena; one explanation offered is that they are porous coral/pumice. Identity CONFIRMED as the Panchmukhi Hanuman shrine at Rameswaram - not a CSV error. Note: antiquity claims and the relocation story rest on travel press and temple lore only, not on dated records; opening-hour sources conflict (6 a.m.-7 p.m. vs 6 a.m.-1 p.m./4-8 p.m.). Coordinates are geocoder-matched to the temple name on Thulasi Bawa Madam Street, Thangachimadam - slight uncertainty.

name: Panchmukhi Hanuman Temple
town_description: A smaller Hanuman shrine on the outskirts of Rameswaram town, about 2 km from the main Ramanathaswamy Temple toward Thangachimadam; a standard stop on the Rameswaram temple circuit.

travel.airport: Madurai airport is the nearest major airport (distance verify)
travel.railway: Rameswaram railway station; auto/taxi from the main temple
travel.road: About 2 km from the Rameswaram temple on the road toward Thangachimadam; easily reached by auto or taxi

visitor_information.best_time: October to April; early mornings or late afternoons to avoid peak crowds
